overview: Human Geography of India and AP: 43 official questions (2008–2024), almost all one-liners with Census figures. Demographics (20) and human-development indices (11) dominate, then urbanisation (8); tribal, racial and religious groups are thin and migration/linguistic groups not yet asked. AP Census numbers (literacy, SC/ST %, district extremes) are a recurring angle.

possibility.angle: Human development – HDI components, related indices (MPI, IHDI, GDI/GEM, HCI), AP vs India HDI
possibility.what_they_ask: What is / is not a component of HDI, which index replaced which, income measure (PPP), poorest State in MPI, % change in India's HDI (time-sensitive).

possibility.angle: Demographics – Census growth phases, sex ratio, literacy, workers, demographic dividend, AP figures
possibility.what_they_ask: Year of great divide, explosion period, State with lowest sex ratio, AP literacy/SC%/child sex ratio, main-worker days, dividend age group.

possibility.angle: Urbanisation – causes, AP urban share, State rankings, functional classes of towns
possibility.what_they_ask: Least urbanised southern State, rural:urban ratio of AP, highest urban growth, town–function matching, first UDA.
Natural targets from Census style: main reason for female migration (marriage) vs male (work), dominant stream (rural–rural), push vs pull factors, largest out-migrating States.
Names of racial/mixed groups (Amerind, Mestizo, Mulatto).

possibility.angle: Tribal groups – tribe–State matching, AP ST districts
possibility.what_they_ask: Tribe → State/UT, AP district with highest ST population.
State with the highest share of a religion (proportion vs absolute).
Natural targets: language families (Indo-Aryan largest, Dravidian second), Eighth Schedule count (22), Telugu as second/fourth most spoken by Census, classical-language status.

traps.trap: Inserts an indicator from another index as an HDI component [index mix]
traps.spot: 'not a component of HDI' with IMR, assets or inequality
traps.fix: HDI = life expectancy + education (mean and expected years of schooling) + income (GNI/GDP per capita PPP). IMR → PQLI; assets → MPI; inequality loss → IHDI.
traps.pyq: Not in HDI → Infant mortality rate [group2-2008-paper3#21]; → Ownership of basic assets [prelims-2017#145]; → loss due to inequality [mains-2017-paper3#30]

traps.trap: Offers market exchange rate instead of PPP
traps.fix: HDI always uses purchasing power parity dollars.
traps.pyq: → GDP per capita US$ in PPP [group2-2008-paper3#133]

traps.trap: Shifts the Census growth phase by one block
traps.fix: 1901-21 stagnant; 1921 year of great divide; 1921-51 steady growth; 1951-81 explosion; after 1981 high but slowing.

traps.trap: Gives a neighbouring north-Indian State for the lowest sex ratio
traps.fix: Census 2011 lowest State sex ratio = Haryana (879); highest = Kerala (1084).

traps.trap: Defines demographic dividend by a wrong driver
traps.spot: Options on skills, women's work or child population
traps.fix: It is growth from a rising working-age share (15-59 in Indian usage).
traps.pyq: → rise in share of working people [mains-2017-paper3#40]; age group 15-59 [prelims-2019#117]

traps.trap: Swaps town examples between functional classes
traps.fix: NCERT: Ankleshwar = mining (oil); Jamshedpur = industrial; Gandhinagar = administrative; Udhampur = garrison.

traps.trap: Moves a tribe to a neighbouring hill State
traps.fix: Gaddi – Himachal; Bhutia – Sikkim; Jarawa – Andaman; Santhal – Jharkhand.

traps.spot: 'highest proportion' of a group with a populous State as option
traps.fix: Proportion: Himachal has the highest Hindu share; UP has the largest number.

techniques.name: Three-dimension test for HDI [component check]
techniques.how: Ask if the option is health, education or income; anything else is not HDI.
techniques.example: Assets fit none of the three → not counted [prelims-2017#145]

techniques.name: Census ladder for numbers
techniques.how: Keep the decade sequence; the answer is usually the latest value, the others are earlier decades.

techniques.name: Index succession
techniques.how: Remember HDR 2010 replacements: MPI replaced HPI; GII replaced GDI/GEM.

techniques.name: AP below-India check
techniques.how: For AP vs India demographic comparisons, AP is lower in growth and was below India on HDI in NHDR 2001.
techniques.example: AP 1991-2001 growth → less than India [group2-2008-paper3#83]; AP HDI 2001 → less than India [group2-2008-paper3#101]

techniques.name: AP district extremes card
techniques.how: Memorise AP 2011 extremes: lowest literacy Vizianagaram, highest ST Visakhapatnam, most rural population East Godavari.

techniques.name: Anchor-pair matching
techniques.how: Lock one obvious pair, then eliminate codes.
techniques.example: Jarawa–Andaman (b-III) leaves only 'a-IV, b-III, c-II, d-I' [prelims-2024#50]

confusions.remember: UNDP health-education-income vs World Bank survival-school-health.
MPI (2010) replaced HPI; MPI counts deprivations incl. assets.
1995 gender indices replaced by GII in 2010.
PQLI (Morris) uses IMR, literacy, life expectancy at age one; HDI uses income.
183 days or more vs less than 183 days.
Year of great divide vs population explosion.
Goa most urbanised; growth rankings differ – read which one is asked.
Mining (oil) town vs industrial town in NCERT classes.

anchors: Census 2011 India sex ratio 943; Kerala 1084 highest; Haryana 879 lowest State.
1921 – year of the great divide; 1951-81 – population explosion.
HDR 2010 – MPI replaced HPI; GII replaced GDI/GEM; IHDI introduced.
Global MPI 2018 – 271 million moved out of poverty (2005-06 to 2015-16); Bihar poorest.
AP 2001 – population ~7.6 crore, female literacy ~50%, urban share ~27%.
Residual AP 2011 – SC 17.08%, ST 5.53%; lowest literacy Vizianagaram; highest ST Visakhapatnam.
AP least urbanised southern State in 2011.
Demographic dividend – working-age share (15-59) rising; India median age ~29 (2020).
checklist: HDI item? Ask: health, education or income – otherwise it belongs to another index.
Proportion or absolute number? Level or growth rate?
Which Census year and which AP (undivided or 13-district)?
Place decade figures on the Census ladder before choosing.
For tribes and towns, lock one sure pair first.
Time-sensitive index ranks: answer per the report named in the stem.
